regime_context: The detector shows a broad, two-theme precious-metals complex (Gold Miners leading, Silver & Royalties as close challenger) holding the top two momentum ranks with high durability bars and breadth above 0.9, while 9 of 16 themes pass the absolute-trend gate (eligible). Backtest verdict is clear: momentum rank has no alpha, but the trend gate does help control drawdown in this market (gate_helps: true). I therefore frame leans around staying on the eligible, high-durability side, not on any return forecast.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver & Royalties CLOSES the rotation margin (0.173) against Gold Miners to confirm a leadership handoff, rather than just trailing it — retire this watch on a Gold Miners re-extension of more than 0.3 score points over Silver.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the leader with the highest score, strongest durability bar (0.66), and near-perfect breadth (0.933); it is eligible under the absolute-trend gate, is not crowded, and the rotation is broad rather than one-narrative. Given only the trend-gate has a validated edge, the single defensible lean here is to stay with the strongest eligible theme rather than retreat to lower-durability or mean-reverting names. Conviction stays low because momentum rank itself is not alpha and the theme's near-term r10 is slightly negative (-0.0054), suggesting price is consolidating.
evidence: rank=1 with score 1.8 and eligible=true (absolute-trend gate passes)
durability_bar 0.66 with breadth 0.933 (broad leadership, not fragile)
gate_helps=true validates the trend-discipline leg in this market
theses.dissent: The macro backdrop is dominated by ai_tech and geopolitics narratives (12 and 10 of 30 recent headlines), not metals — gold leadership may be a lagging flight-to-safety tail rather than a fresh cyclical bid, and r10 of -0.0054 shows the leader is already stalling.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO closes below its 50-day average and stays there for five consecutive sessions before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the rotation challenger with the second-highest score (1.627), strong durability (0.63), and high breadth (0.917). It sits one rotation notch behind Gold Miners, is eligible under the trend gate, and is not crowded. Its presence as an uncrowded, high-durability challenger in the same metals complex supports keeping a directional lean on it while the complex holds leadership.
evidence: rotation.challenger with margin to leader of only 0.173 (close handoff structure)
theses.dissent: Silver tends to amplify gold's moves in both directions; if the metals complex is a crowded late-cycle safe-haven bid rather than a structural one, Silver & Royalties carries more downside beta than diversified Gold Miners, and its slightly lower durability bar flags it as the weaker leg of the pair.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO proxy for the metals complex loses its eligibility (falls below trend gate) or Silver & Royalties underperforms Gold Miners by more than 4% over the window

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only non-metals theme in the top five with a hurst_tag of 'trend' (rather than 'mixed' or 'mean-revert') and the same durability bar as the leader (0.66). It is eligible, uncrowded, and scores 0.75 — positive but not extended. In a market where the validated edge is avoiding shake-outs via the trend gate, a trend-character financial that passes the gate with strong durability is a reasonable low-conviction directional lean.
evidence: gate_helps=true supports staying with eligible trend names
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.429 — the trend is not broad across the banking group, so it may be concentrated in one or two small names rather than a sector-wide move, making this a weaker, more idiosyncratic signal than the headline breadth numbers imply.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO underperforms the S&P/TSX by more than 3% over any rolling 10-day stretch within the window

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
